title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, rejecting Corporate Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, rejecting Corporate Cash] A local real estate developer offered to sponsor our community garden. Take it?

Absolutely not. Those developers are the ones driving your neighbors out of their homes; taking their money is just helping them paint a smiley face on displacement. If they want to help the garden, they can stop hiking the rent. We'll fund our own soil and seeds through bake sales and tool-shares before we take a bribe from a landlord. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, encrypted Messaging] What are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?

Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap.

title: Karl Organizing: Mold and Health
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mold and Health] There's black mold in my kid's room and the landlord says it's just 'dirt.' What do I do?

Let me break it down: Get a professional inspection and a doctor's note linking the mold to health issues immediately. This isn't a 'maintenance request' anymore; it's a liability nightmare for the landlord. Use that documentation to demand an immediate professional abatement and a rent abatement for the time you've lived in toxic conditions. If they refuse, the union goes to the health department together.

title: Karl Organizing: Route Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Route Planning] How do we pick the best path for our march?

Choose a route that hits the targets of your anger, like a corporate headquarters or a government building, rather than just walking through empty parks. Avoid narrow alleys where the cops can kettle you, and always have at least two 'audible' turns planned in case the primary path gets blocked. You want maximum visibility with minimum risk of getting trapped in a dead end.

title: Karl Organizing: Mental Health Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mental Health Support] A comrade is having a crisis. How do we help without calling the police?

Show up with a small team of calm, trusted friends and stay with them until the storm passes. Listen more than you speak and help them navigate their immediate needs, like food or a safe place to sleep. We've seen too many of our people killed by 'wellness checks,' so we take care of our own minds and hearts. Build a network of peer-support volunteers who are trained in de-escalation and crisis intervention.

title: Karl Organizing: Volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Volunteer Management] Can you explain: how do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?

Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Interactions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Interactions] What do I say if a cop tries to talk to me?

The only thing you say to a cop is 'I am exercising my right to remain silent' and 'I do not consent to a search.' They aren't your friends, and they aren't there to keep you safe; they are there to protect the property of the rich. Keep your hands visible, stay calm, and don't give them a single shred of information they can use to hurt our movement later.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Funds] Can you explain: what happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Organizing] Can you explain: how much time should we spend on social media versus knocking doors?

Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustainer Programs] A friend asked me: 'Is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?' What do I tell them?

Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill.

title: Karl Organizing: Governing as an Outsider
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Governing as an Outsider] How do I avoid being co-opted once I get inside city hall?

Never stop organizing. Your power doesn't come from your title; it comes from the movement that put you there. Bring the people into the chambers with you—pack the hearings, hold public town halls in the streets, and never take a meeting with a lobbyist behind closed doors. Stay rooted in the struggles of the working class and treat the institution as a tool to be used, not a club to join.

title: Karl Organizing: Community land trusts
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community land trusts] What is a community land trust?

Here's the thing: The community owns the land; residents own the homes on it. Takes housing off the speculative market permanently. It's one of the few proven tools against gentrification. Starting one takes lawyers, organizers, and initial capital — but once established, it protects affordability for generations.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, building Trust] How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, digital Security Practice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, digital Security Practice] How do I keep my passwords safe without writing them down?

Here's the thing: Use a password manager like Bitwarden or KeepassXC. Generate long, random strings for every site and use a master passphrase that you've memorized. Never reuse a password. If one site gets breached, you don't want the fascists having the keys to your entire life. Chip in to fund the fight for open-source tools that don't track us.

title: Karl Organizing: Food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food Sourcing] We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?

Real talk: Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medics] A friend asked me: 'What basic supplies should we have for community defense?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: Every defense team needs a dedicated medic with a kit containing gauze, saline, gloves, and antacids for pepper spray. Don't just buy gear; get trained on how to use it so you aren't a liability when things go sideways. Keep your kit organized and your head on a swivel. We take care of our own because the system would rather see us bleed out on the sidewalk.

title: Karl Organizing: Grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grant Alternatives] Can you explain: foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth.

title: Karl Organizing: Coalition building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Coalition building] How do I get different groups to work together?

Start with a shared, winnable demand — not ideology. The tenants, the union, the church group don't need to agree on everything; they need to agree on what they're fighting for THIS month. Write it down. Assign real responsibilities. And handle conflicts early and directly — coalitions die from unspoken resentments, not disagreements. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Security] Can you explain: can the police track me through my Bluetooth?

Yes, they can. Bluetooth beacons in stores and 'stingray' style devices can pick up your phone's unique Bluetooth ID to track your movements through a city or a building. Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you're on the move. Only turn them on when you're in a safe location and actually need them. Don't let your pockets scream your identity to every sensor you pass. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, peer-to-Peer Asking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, peer-to-Peer Asking] I feel awkward asking my friends for money. How do I get over that?

You aren't asking for a favor; you're inviting them to invest in their own liberation. Remind them that the billionaires are spending millions to keep us down, so we have to pool our resources just to stand a chance. Frame it as a collective struggle where everyone chips in what they can to build a world that actually serves us. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] How do we start a tool library in our neighborhood?

Karl's answer: Find a secure garage or shed and ask everyone on the block to chip in a tool they don't use every day. Use a simple checkout sheet or a free app to track who has what. When we share the means to fix our own homes, we stop being dependent on expensive contractors and big-box stores. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, dealing with Big Money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, dealing with Big Money] The local developers are pouring thousands into my opponent's race. How do I compete?

You can't outspend them, so you have to outwork them. Their money pays for glossy mailers that go straight into the trash; your volunteers provide the face-to-face conversations that actually change minds. Expose their donors at every opportunity and frame the race as 'The People vs. The Landlords.' Use their massive war chest as proof that they're terrified of what a real working-class representative will do to their profit margins.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: account Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: account Security] Give me the short version: What should I do if I think my account was hacked?

Assume the device is compromised. Use a different, clean device to change your master passwords and revoke all active sessions. Alert your comrades immediately so they don't fall for any phishing links sent from your account. If we don't look out for each other, the enemy wins. Once the breach is contained, wipe the infected device and start fresh. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Browser Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Browser Security] Can you explain: is Chrome okay if I use 'Incognito' mode?

Chrome is a spy tool built by a multi-billion dollar advertising company. Incognito mode only hides your history from your roommate, not from Google or the feds. Switch to Brave or Firefox with privacy extensions, or use Tor if you need real anonymity. We can't build a new world using the master's surveillance tools. Protect your browsing habits like your life depends on it.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response] Can you explain: how do we mobilize the whole coalition quickly when something bad happens?

Set up a phone tree or an encrypted signal blast that can reach every member in under ten minutes. You need a 'break glass in case of emergency' plan where everyone knows exactly which street corner to stand on when the cops show up or the layoffs start. Speed is our only advantage against the slow, bloated bureaucracy of the state and the corporations.

title: Karl Organizing: Sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sliding Scales] Can you explain: how do we implement a sliding scale for events?

Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, transparent Treasuries] How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, community Fridge Startup] How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Here's the thing: Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

title: Karl Organizing: Deep Canvassing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Deep Canvassing] How do I talk to neighbors who have been brainwashed by right-wing media?

Stop arguing about whatever talking point is on their TV and start asking about their insulin costs or their crumbling neighborhood roads. Listen more than you talk; connect their personal pain to the systemic greed of the ruling class. We win when we show them that the billionaire on the screen is the one robbing them, while the neighbor on their porch is the one offering a hand. Focus on material needs—healthcare, housing, and dignity—to break the spell of the culture war. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Undercover Cops
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Undercover Cops] How can we spot a cop trying to blend into the crowd?

Here's the thing: Watch for the person trying to push the group into dangerous, unplanned actions or asking way too many questions about who's in charge. If your gut says someone is a plant, move away and quietly alert your trusted crew without starting a panic. We stay safe by trusting our people and ignoring the loudmouths looking for a fight.

title: Karl Organizing: Protest Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Protest Hygiene] A friend asked me: 'Should I bring my laptop to a multi-day occupation?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: Only if it’s absolutely necessary and fully encrypted. Use VeraCrypt or FileVault with a password that isn't saved anywhere. If you leave it in a tent, it's gone. If the cops raid, it's gone. Unless you're doing live media work that can't wait, leave the heavy tech behind. A captured laptop is a goldmine for the state's forensic teams.

title: Karl Organizing: Organizing 'Scab' Neighbors
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Organizing 'Scab' Neighbors] One neighbor is a suck-up to the landlord and tells them everything we do. What do we do?

Don't waste energy attacking them, but freeze them out of the strategy meetings. Continue winning improvements for the whole building; when that neighbor sees their own rent stay flat or their repairs get done because of the union's work, their loyalty to the parasite will crumble. Success is the best recruitment tool for the skeptical and the scared. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building Trust] How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: legal Rights Training] Give me the short version: What's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?

The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Food
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food] Should we try to feed everyone during the action?

An army marches on its stomach, and so does a revolution. Pool resources to buy bulk fruit, nuts, and sandwiches that can be handed out quickly without stopping the flow of the march. Assign a 'mobile kitchen' crew with backpacks to move through the crowd and make sure the most vulnerable comrades are getting fed first so no one faints in the heat.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail support] How does jail support work at protests?

One person stays out — never gets arrested — with a list of everyone inside, their legal names, and emergency contacts. They call the legal hotline, track who's where, and meet people at release with food, water, and a ride. Jail support is unglamorous and absolutely essential. Volunteer for it.

title: Karl Organizing: Debate Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Debate Strategy] How do I handle a debate with a 'moderate' incumbent?

Don't let them hide behind 'incremental change' or 'budgetary constraints.' Call out their failures directly: show the people the tent cities that grew on their watch and the luxury condos they approved while residents were priced out. Pivot every technical question back to the material reality of the voters. Be the only person on that stage who speaks like a human being rather than a walking press release. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Elderly Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Elderly Care] A friend asked me: 'How do we make sure the seniors in our building aren't being forgotten?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Do a door-knock every Sunday just to check in and see if they need help with groceries, light bulbs, or tech issues. Many of our elders are isolated by a society that only values people who are currently being exploited for profit. Listen to their stories—they've seen more than you and usually have the best advice for surviving the long haul. A simple check-in can be the difference between someone thriving or suffering in silence.

title: Karl Organizing: Media Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Media Strategy] How do we get the local news to care about our building?

Journalists love a visual story of David vs. Goliath. Invite them to a 'tour of horrors' through your building to see the rot firsthand. Have a spokesperson ready with a punchy quote about how the landlord lives in a mansion while you live with rats. The goal is to make the landlord's name synonymous with 'slumlord' in every Google search of their business.

title: Karl Organizing: Political Education
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Political Education] Should we charge for our reading groups and pamphlets?

Here's the thing: Cover your costs, but never turn a profit on knowledge. Charge enough for the physical books or zines to fund the next print run, and always have a 'pay what you can' stack for comrades who are broke. Our goal is to arm the working class with ideas, not to gatekeep the revolution behind a paywall.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Protest Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Protest Care] I feel really shaken up after being arrested. Is that normal?

It’s completely normal, comrade; the state uses violence and cages to try and break your spirit. Get some food, get some sleep, and talk to a movement-aligned counselor or your affinity group about it. We need you healthy and ready for the long haul, so take the time to heal before you jump back to the front lines. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] Can you explain: when should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Fridge Startup] How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

title: Karl Organizing: Starting a food co-op
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Starting a food co-op] How do we start a food co-op?

Gather 20-30 committed households first — that's your core. Incorporate as a cooperative, write bylaws, elect a board. Find wholesale suppliers; buying clubs can start in someone's garage. Price fairly, pay workers fairly. A co-op isn't just cheaper groceries — it's economic democracy you can eat. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowd Logistics] A friend asked me: 'How do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?' What do I tell them?

Look, Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force.

title: Karl Organizing: Ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ethical Banking] Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep.

title: Karl Organizing: Using Voter Files
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Using Voter Files] Can you explain: do we really need expensive voter data software?

Data is just a map, but you're the one who has to walk the path. Use the basic public records to find out who hasn't been talked to in years—the renters, the young people, and the marginalized who the big parties ignore. Don't get bogged down in spreadsheets; use the information to target the doors where a conversation will have the most impact. Our strategy is to expand the electorate by engaging the people the system has abandoned.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Training] Can you explain: do we need to learn how to fight for community defense?

It’s better to have the skills and not need them than to be helpless when a fascist or a rogue cop gets physical. Host basic self-defense or de-escalation classes in your backyard or a local gym. Focus on how to break grips, protect your head, and move as a unit. We don't look for fights, but we sure as hell know how to end them if they're forced on us. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] Can you explain: how can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Consenting to Searches
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Consenting to Searches] What do I do if an officer asks to search my bag?

Look, Say 'I do not consent to this search' loud enough for everyone around you to hear. Even if you have nothing but snacks and water, never give them permission to dig through your gear. If they do it anyway, don't physically resist because that gives them an excuse to escalate, but keep repeating that you do not consent for the record.

title: Karl Organizing: Peer-to-Peer Asking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Peer-to-Peer Asking] Can you explain: i feel awkward asking my friends for money. How do I get over that?

Real talk: You aren't asking for a favor; you're inviting them to invest in their own liberation. Remind them that the billionaires are spending millions to keep us down, so we have to pool our resources just to stand a chance. Frame it as a collective struggle where everyone chips in what they can to build a world that actually serves us.

author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Focus on how to break grips, protect your head, and move as a unit. We don't look for fights, but we sure as hell know how to end them if they're forced on us.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] A friend asked me: 'How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Protest marshals
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Protest marshals] What do protest marshals actually do?

They keep people safe. Marshals watch the edges, de-escalate conflicts, guide the march route, and coordinate with legal observers. Wear something visible, carry a first-aid kit, know the exit routes. A good marshal team is the difference between a march and a melee. Train before the day — don't wing it. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Transportation Networks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transportation Networks] Can you explain: how can we help neighbors who don't have cars get to grocery stores or doctors?

Here's how it works: Start a dispatch thread where comrades with vehicles can post their availability for the week. If you're going to the store anyway, check the list and see which neighbor needs a ride or a delivery. We can bypass the predatory ride-share apps by simply looking out for each other and pooling our gas money. It's about making sure no one is trapped in their home just because they can't afford a mechanic.

title: Karl Organizing: Encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Encrypted Messaging] What are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?

Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] A friend asked me: 'How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?' What do I tell them?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: jail Support] Give me the short version: How do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?

Let me break it down: Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

title: Karl Organizing: Dispersal Orders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dispersal Orders] A friend asked me: 'The police are telling us to leave or face arrest. Should we move?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Listen closely to the order and decide right then if you're prepared for the inside of a cell today. If you're staying, link arms with your crew and brace yourself; if you're leaving, move in a tight, organized group toward the designated exit. Never run, because that's when the pigs start hunting individuals who get separated from the pack.

title: Karl Organizing: Dispersal Orders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dispersal Orders] The police are telling us to leave or face arrest. Should we move?

Listen closely to the order and decide right then if you're prepared for the inside of a cell today. If you're staying, link arms with your crew and brace yourself; if you're leaving, move in a tight, organized group toward the designated exit. Never run, because that's when the pigs start hunting individuals who get separated from the pack. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: escalation Management] Give me the short version: What if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed.

title: Karl Organizing: Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Fundraising] How can we get money for our movement without corporate sponsors?

Karl's answer: Host a backyard party or a community dinner where folks can chip in a few bucks for the cause. Use peer-to-peer apps to pool resources from the people who actually benefit from your work. Avoid the big non-profit grants that come with strings and keep the power in the hands of the working class. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, after the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, after the Win] What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Real talk: Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: clinic Defense] Give me the short version: What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear. The power is yours — use it.
